ReAct loop plus a validation agent, but the reported claims are execution accuracy on BIRD (77.84%) and Spider (89.75%); nothing measured about the loop itself.
Contribution is GEM, a four-stage trajectory data-synthesis pipeline plus an SFT synthesizer; claims are BFCL V3 benchmark gains, not anything about loop control.
Open-source training data and QA/trajectory synthesis for a ReAct search agent; claims are BrowseComp and xbench scores, no evidence about the loop mechanism.
HGPO is a stepwise advantage-estimation scheme for agentic RL training; evidence is success rates on ALFWorld and WebShop, not a claim about the runtime loop.
ReTree traces back to the node introducing a contradicted claim, prunes branches and resumes search; compared against Full-Trajectory ReAct with per-step context measured: loop state.
Solver-Critic-Selector system with confidence-based compute allocation, but the reported claims are SOTA results on HLE, GAIA and XBench; the mechanism itself is never measured.
Proposes interacting with multiple environments per step with cross-trajectory sharing and compares this parallel paradigm against sequential reason-then-act baselines: iteration policy.
Causal localization over a dependency graph picks the root-cause module for reflection-based repair, beating context-filtering baselines: retry/repair.
OS-Symphony is an authored CUA framework (Orchestrator, reflection-memory, tool agents) whose claims are SOTA benchmark numbers such as 65.84% on OSWorld.
BranPO is a branch-sampling credit-assignment method for agentic RL training; the reported evidence is multi-hop QA benchmark gains, not a claim about loop control.
Studies entropy dynamics of agent RL training and adds the SEAL auxiliary loss; claims are training stability and downstream benchmark performance, not the agent's control loop.
A meta agent searches harness adaptations (instructions, tools, orchestration loops) from failure trajectories, compared per pair over 21 task-SLM pairs: iteration policy as studied variable.
AgentJet is distributed training infrastructure; the server-client topology is a training deployment concern and the claim is a 6.25x actor-update speedup, not loop control.
Benchmark auditing the process, not just answers: five reasoning nodes measuring diagnosis updating and contradiction-based self-correction under stressors: verification.
CoEvoKG writes verified evidence back into a knowledge graph for self-play training; the reported claims are macro-average QA accuracy gains over base models and RL baselines.
Explicitly a review of the LLM landscape and theoretical explanations for generalization capacity; a secondary study with no method.
25,000 runs decompose scaffold vs base-model variance (1.5% vs 41.4%) and measure refutation-driven belief revision at 26%, evidence ignored in 68% of traces: verification.
Recursive Tournament Voting and Parallel-Distill-Refine are compared as parallel vs sequential test-time scaling over rollout summaries, framing scaling as selection and reuse: iteration policy.
ReSum periodically condenses interaction history so exploration can continue past the context limit, and is compared directly against the ReAct loop paradigm (+4.5%): loop state.
Self-described survey with a taxonomy of LLM intervention operators in the RL loop; a secondary study retained only as a snowballing seed.
RTPO is a reverse-turn credit-assignment formulation for stabilizing multi-turn RL training; evidence is 21.50% and 10.76% gains over baselines, not a claim about the runtime loop.
Benchmark record of 200 multiple-choice geochemistry questions reporting aggregate accuracy and item retention; no loop property such as stuck loops, termination or retries is measured.
Report on SFT data-synthesis modifications (graph size, tool set, low-step filtering) for a stock ReAct agent; claims are benchmark scores such as 46.0% on BrowseComp.
M-ASK splits search from knowledge management, but the reported claims are answer accuracy on multi-hop QA plus training stability: a multi-agent system beating baselines on a task.
SWE-World replaces containerized execution with a learned surrogate for training and evaluation; the claims are SWE-bench Verified scores rising from 6.2% to 68.2%.
Orchard is an environment service plus three training recipes; the reported evidence is SOTA benchmark results (69.7% SWE-bench, 68.4% GUI, 59.6% Claw-Eval).
AgentMeter scores LM-CLI pairs on budget sensitivity and zero-reward execution and shows no CLI harness is universally optimal, making the harness the studied variable: termination/budget.
Explicitly a survey of the Model Context Protocol architecture and challenges; secondary study with no method.
Argues harness design is a first-class ML problem, formalizes harness configuration search, and reports a controlled manual-tuning case study against an end-to-end HARBOR run: iteration policy.
KernelSkill is a multi-agent framework with dual-level memory whose reported claims are 100% success on KernelBench and speedups over Torch Eager: task outcomes.
The studied variable is the diffusion vs autoregressive backbone inside a fixed agent workflow, with end-to-end speed and accuracy claims; no loop mechanism is contributed.
Trajectory summarization compresses history into state updates that drive the next decision, measured against baselines by success rate and 58.7% token cut: loop state.
WebGym contributes 300k training tasks, an RL recipe and a fast rollout system; claims are out-of-distribution success rate rising from 26.2% to 42.9%.
Self-described comprehensive survey of MCP architecture, implementations and open challenges; a secondary study.
AgentEvolver's self-questioning, self-navigating and self-attributing are evaluated by exploration efficiency and sample utilization against RL baselines: training efficiency, not loop control.
Attacks the restriction of retrieval to episode initiation by generating short-term strategy memory on the fly, compared against static-memory baselines across compute levels: loop state.
PRISMA 2020-compliant systematic literature review screening 2,387 records to 60 studies, producing a taxonomy and maturity framework: a secondary study.
STRIATUM-CTF is an authored MCP-based agentic framework whose headline evidence is winning a live CTF against 21 human teams: task outcome.
Source-code study of 13 coding-agent scaffolds finds five composable loop primitives (ReAct, generate-test-repair, plan-execute, retry, tree search): iteration policy.
Self-organizing agent teams evaluated by BioML-Bench leaderboard percentile, training speedups and Spearman correlation: a multi-agent system beating baselines on domain tasks.
Argues the context-overload vs pruning trade-off comes from centralized memory organization and decouples gist accumulation from the Planner, measuring accuracy against overhead: loop state.
The delegation harness is used to generate SFT trajectories, and the reported claims are BrowseComp 68.1 and BrowseComp-ZH 73.3 for the resulting model: task outcomes.
Self-described survey of terminal agents organizing architecture, competence acquisition and evaluation; retained as a snowballing seed.
ProGPO is a step-level grouping and advantage-estimation method for agentic RL; evidence is gains over matched RL baselines on ALFWorld and WebShop, not the runtime loop.
